revisionLevel: short-form (use for Revision 1/2/3/Final passes, not first-time learning)
coreIdea: Cache = small fast memory exploiting locality of reference. Reduces AMAT.
mustRememberFormulas: tag bits + index/set bits + offset bits = total address bits (ALWAYS check this)
AMAT = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty (recurse for multi-level, work from last level backward)

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: cache size + block size + associativity + address width, asked for TAG/SET/WORD bits
multi-level hit rates + access times, asked for average access time
sequence of block references + replacement policy, asked what's in cache / miss count
C code with nested loop over 2D array, asked which order is cache-friendly
TRUE/FALSE statements about write-through/write-back/inclusion, no numbers

commonTrapsQuickList: Local vs global miss rate — check which one the question defines before using AMAT recursion
Inclusion property direction: L1 ⊆ L2, not the reverse
KB/MB = powers of 2 (2^10, 2^20), not 1000/1000000, unless question says otherwise
highYieldPyqLessons: Address-split questions are ~25% of all Cache Memory PYQs — this is the single highest-ROI sub-skill to drill.
Post-2014 questions increasingly combine two patterns in one question (e.g., address-split + AMAT, or loop-locality + address-split) — practice combining, not just isolated patterns.
